story.title: THE DAY WREN WAS RIGHT
story.deck: A floating market of twelve hundred households has thirty days to meet a sanitation law it genuinely breaks, and the plan that would save it is wrong in the one way only Wren could see.
story.shape: A rebuild in six scenes: the clean plan fails on a companion's objection, a hand-kept ledger turns out to be the system itself with three holes, a sealed-prediction sampling beats the loud rival cause, a council decides what each party will and will not give, two excluded households keep their objections, and the water reads the result while the lease and the ledger stay in different hands.

scenes.title: The Clean Plan
paragraphs: *Harbour Office quay, Sorrel Water · Day 3 of 30, 08:10*
The Order was fourteen pages long and gave thirty days, and on the third morning Illuminara laid her answer across the Harbour Office counter on a single sheet.

Twelve hundred boat-households lived on Kettle Market. The Harbourmaster's Sanitation Order No. 14 said that after the fifteenth of November none of them could go on discharging into Sorrel Water, and the August samples had shown the Order was right. Illuminara's sheet showed a licensed pump-out barge, six fixed stops, a sensor in every tank and one monthly bill.

**Cedric Aldana**  
It is the cleanest compliance plan anyone has put in front of me. Every vessel metered, every pump-out logged. I could sign it on a Friday.
Wren Odira came up the quay steps with smoke in her coat and river mud to the knee. She had spent three weeks sleeping on other people's decks. She read the sheet standing, twice, and set it down.

**Wren Odira**  
It will fail.

**Illuminara**  
Tell me where it breaks first.

**Wren Odira**  
Wherever the barge is when the string has moved. Kettle doesn't sit at six stops. It re-rafts on every ebb, boats slide to be near the boats they owe. Your stop six holds a hundred and forty hulls on Monday and sixty on Thursday. And you meter the tank. Whoever pays by the tank learns to keep it half empty and the hose long.

**Illuminara**  
A meter that pays a family to leave the harbour dirty. I did not model that.

**Wren Odira**  
You modelled a machine. It's a rumour with a rota.
Illuminara did not defend the sheet. *Wren has the shape of it. I do not yet have one fact that is worth more than her three weeks.*

**Illuminara**  
Then something is already working. In August the water was bad, not lethal, and Kettle has lived on it for thirty years. Who keeps the record of how?

**Wren Odira**  
There's a book.

**Cedric Aldana**  
The Order wants a record for each vessel. A book is not a record.

**Illuminara**  
Then I would like to read the book before I tell you what a record is.

scenes.title: The Tie-Book
paragraphs: *Dock-mistress's counter, Kettle Market · Day 4, 06:00*
Odalys Ferreira kept eleven volumes of the tie-book under her counter, in pencil, because ink runs on a wet quay. She laid the current one open and kept one hand flat on it.

**Odalys Ferreira**  
You may read here. You may not copy a page, and if I see you reading a name you weren't asked to, I close it. This book is the only thing on the water that nobody has ever been able to buy.

Illuminara read for six hours. *Selka carried Reed 3, 5, 7. Tues. Pump to Mill 2, from Mabuya, back by dusk. Tied: Aurelian, visitor.* Line by line she let the entries fall into place as a graph: strings of rafted boats, carriers who wheeled the waste to the barge quay on days each string had chosen, pumps that travelled on a promise.
Nobody had written down a rota. The book was the rota, kept in the one language the market trusted.

**Illuminara**  
Eight boats in ten pass their waste to a carrier, the carrier takes it to the licensed quay, and the book shows eleven years of corrections. Thirty-eight strings, and none has ever asked the Harbourmaster for anything.

**Wren Odira**  
I told you.

**Illuminara**  
You did, and you were right about the form. It fails in three places, and I find them by what the book leaves out. First, Reed Row. Tuesdays and Fridays, every week for eleven years. Not one carry on a Sunday.

**Odalys Ferreira**  
Sunday is rest. Reed Row rests hardest of any string.

**Illuminara**  
Second. Every pump loan in this volume names Mabuya or Mabuya's spare. One pump, one owner, who is seventy-nine.

**Odalys Ferreira**  
Gwil Anand will outlive the harbour.

**Illuminara**  
Third, and it is the one the Inspector cares about. Nothing here lets the Order learn that any of this happened without opening the book to him.

**Odalys Ferreira**  
That is what the book is for.

**Illuminara**  
I know. I will come back to it. But the first two I only suspect. The book cannot tell me whether Reed Row's Sunday waste goes into the water, and half this harbour will say the water is dirty because of the tannery drain upstream.

**Wren Odira**  
They'll say it before you've finished the sentence.

**Illuminara**  
Then we measure before anyone claims anything.

scenes.title: Three Stations
paragraphs: *Sorrel Water, on the ebb · Saturday 22:00 to Monday 06:00*
Pia Zane, who ran the Inspector's small laboratory out of a van, set four sample stations and was told by Illuminara which results would count against her.

Illuminara wrote the predictions on a card, sealed it, and gave it to Aldana before the first bottle was filled. If the Sunday gap was real, Reed Row's mouth would run at least five times its Saturday reading on the Sunday ebb while the station above the market stayed flat. If the tannery was the cause, the upstream station would be high on both nights and Reed Row would barely differ from it. If neither, everything would be flat and she would have been wrong about the book.

**Hesper Quill**  
You are sampling Reed Row on our day of rest. You will write our shame in water and hand it to the Inspector.

**Illuminara**  
I am sampling the one place your string cannot answer for. If the number is bad on Sunday, it will be the first fact either of us has that is ours to fix.

**Hesper Quill**  
And if it's bad on Saturday too?

**Illuminara**  
Then I am wrong and the card says so.
Wren rowed the bottles herself, one leg of the route at a time. The numbers came back on Monday at six, in enterococci per hundred millilitres.

**Pia Zane**  
Saturday ebb. Upstream, ninety. Reed Row, two hundred and ten. Mid-market, a hundred and eighty. Below the market, two hundred and sixty. Sunday ebb. Upstream, a hundred and ten. Reed Row, two thousand three hundred. Mid-market, six-forty. Below, seven hundred.

**Wren Odira**  
Upstream is flat.

**Pia Zane**  
The tannery adds something after rain. It is not this.

**Illuminara**  
The tannery is a fact and it is not this fact. It will still be there when we finish, and I will say so to the council so that nobody has to hear it from the other side.
Hesper Quill read the Sunday line twice. She did not apologise and she did not argue. She asked what it would cost her people to stop it.

scenes.title: Three Links
paragraphs: *The council deck, Kettle Market · Day 9, 19:00*
Thirty-eight string-wardens came, and Aldana came with his Order folded in his pocket. Illuminara had drawn only three additions to the system they already ran, and she said so first.

**Illuminara**  
I am not bringing you a new system. You have one. I am bringing three links it is missing, and each of you can refuse yours.

**Hesper Quill**  
Reed Row will carry its own Sunday. We will not do it under anybody's name in a book that the Inspector reads.

**Selka Dunmore**  
Tam and I will swap. I take Reed's Sunday and Reed takes my Monday. That's a trade among neighbours. It is not a rota for the Harbour Office.

**Illuminara**  
That is the first link, and it is better than mine. I had a paid Sunday carrier. Yours costs nothing and will outlast any budget.

**Gwil Anand**  
And you want my pump.

**Illuminara**  
I want a second one, floated mid-market, lent only through you. If you fall ill, the loan does not stop. You stay the one people ask.

**Gwil Anand**  
If I'm still the one they ask, I will lend it.
Then Aldana unfolded the Order.

**Cedric Aldana**  
I must have a record for each vessel. I do not make the clause.

**Illuminara**  
Then read the clause again, Inspector. Section six, paragraph b. An equivalent community arrangement may be certified in place of a vessel record, if it is held under a lease, if the water at the outfall meets the standard, and if the body that signs can be inspected without notice. It asks for outcomes and does not ask for names. Measure the water at the three stations, once a month and at random. Odalys signs a count of carries with no boat named. The book never leaves her counter.

**Odalys Ferreira**  
You are telling me to hand the Harbourmaster a number and keep the book.

**Illuminara**  
I am telling you that the number is what he is allowed to ask for.

**Wren Odira**  
And a lease. Ten years. That is a leash, and a short one. In year ten they let go of it and Kettle is a fine.

**Cedric Aldana**  
Ten is what the paragraph permits.

**Illuminara**  
Ten is what the law gives this month. I would rather ask for ten and keep the market alive than ask for thirty and meet the Harbourmaster in court with money Kettle does not have.

**Wren Odira**  
That is your arithmetic. It is not mine.
Illuminara let that stand. The vote was the council's and neither of them could take it from the other.

scenes.title: The Two Boats
paragraphs: *The smokehouse Ember, tied at the east edge · Day 14, dusk*

Torvald Beck's smoke-boat had been a ferry hull once. A holding tank would not fit it. Iliana Dross's Aurelian was registered upriver at Cress Market and had been in the tie-book as *visitor* fourteen times.

**Torvald Beck**  
I have read the plan. It was written for the boats that were already inside the book.

**Iliana Dross**  
My name is in your book fourteen times, and in not one of them as a member. I carry my own waste out of this harbour. I have done it for nine years. I will not be counted by your rota or inspected by your Inspector.

**Illuminara**  
He is right, Iliana. The book holds only those who tie, and I read the market through it. That is a hole in my method, not only in the plan.
She turned to Wren, who had sat on Beck's deck three nights running and eaten his fish.

**Wren Odira**  
I have two requests. That Beck and Dross each sit at the council until the lease is signed. And that the fund pays for whatever Beck needs, because he will not ask.

**Illuminara**  
Beck. A sealed float-tank towed astern of Ember, nineteen hundred marks, built by Gwil's apprentice. It is not elegant. It would work.

**Torvald Beck**  
And my name stays out of the Reed Row sheet.

**Illuminara**  
It was never in it.

**Torvald Beck**  
Then the council can vote on the tank.

**Iliana Dross**  
I tie here eleven days a year. I will not be inspected for the other three hundred and fifty-four.

**Illuminara**  
Then I will not ask you to be counted. A free rinse at the barge quay on any day you tie, with no entry in anyone's book. If the water reads clean in spring, you will know whose doing that was, and you can decide again.
Dross did not say yes. She weighed it the way a woman weighs a rope. In the morning the Aurelian had cast off for Cress Market, with a day-pass in her pocket and her reasons unrevised.

scenes.title: What the Water Said
paragraphs: *The quay and Reed Row · Day 27, 17:00*
The trial had run ten days: Reed Row's Sunday carries, Gwil's second pump on its float, and the Ember's tank, towed astern and humming faintly with a pump of its own.

**Pia Zane**  
Sunday ebb. Upstream, a hundred and five. Reed Row, three hundred and ten. Mid-market, a hundred and seventy. Below the market, one-ninety.

**Cedric Aldana**  
From twenty-three hundred to three hundred ten at the mouth. And downstream from seven hundred to one-ninety.

**Pia Zane**  
The tannery is still adding its share. It is a hundred and five. The standard at the outfall is two hundred.

Aldana read the certificate aloud. It named the Kettle Council as the signing body, ten years as the term, three stations, random sampling and no list of boats. He signed under the line. Hesper Quill signed beneath him. Nobody cheered, because the water was still brown and the standard was still a number on a van.

**Wren Odira**  
I still say ten is a leash.

**Illuminara**  
So do I. What would you change?

**Wren Odira**  
Post the three numbers on the quay every month, where any boat can read them. A lease the whole harbour can read is harder to cancel than one in a drawer.

**Illuminara**  
That is stronger than the clause I wrote. Put it to the council.
Odalys opened the book on the counter. She did not ask for permission and she did not offer to show it. She wrote one line, in pencil.
*Sunday, Reed 7. Carried. Tam.*

**Illuminara**  
May I see the page?

**Odalys Ferreira**  
No. It is not your page.

Illuminara smiled, which was not a thing she often did in front of strangers. Out on the water the ebb ran past the market a little clearer than it had on the day she arrived, and Wren, who had been right on the first morning and would be right about the lease in ten years, stood on the quay and read the numbers aloud to the boats.
